thread:
pagerbot: P1 alert — elevated 95th percentile latency and 502s across eastus-serving pool. paging Mike (oncall).

Mike: I'm on it. joining bridge in 2. creating a quick context note here so we can spin up post-incident items.

ops-bot: Incident declared SEV1 at 1945678901. bridge: https://calls.example.com/bridge/ABC123 :phone: 

Ana: saw the spike too, looks like many requests are hitting a cache miss path after the model rollout at ~1930z. kv-cache evictions are spiking, GC churn high on gpu host 7.

Mike: thanks Ana. can you structure a short timeline? I want to capture first touch for postmortem.

Ana: timeline so far — 19:23z deploy v1.3.2 (model + kernel switch), 19:31z first 95p jump, 19:36z pagerbot threshold breached, 19:38z we pushed a canary rollback to v1.3.1 on 20% hosts, 19:45z errors reduced slightly, 19:58z full rollback initiated, 20:05z 95p back to baseline, 20:12z incident resolved.

Sarah: on the bridge I captured stack traces showing KV lookups failing when sequence length caching tries to reuse invalid pointers. looks like a race in the new packing code path.

Mike: good notes. Incident resolved at 20:12z per ops-bot. we need to do classic post-incident follow-up: 1) schedule postmortem, 2) track remediation tasks, 3) draft customer/statuspage comms. tagging folks.

Jordan: I'll draft the statuspage blurb and an initial customer-facing summary. aim to post an interim status within 2 hours? can we do that?

Lee: yes, ops wants a short statuspage update ASAP referencing degraded performance/resolved and that a full RCA will follow. Jordan, i'll review the blurb.

Jordan: draft for statuspage (please review):
```
Between 19:30 UTC and 20:12 UTC we experienced elevated latency and intermittent 502 errors affecting requests routed to the eastus serving pool. The root cause is being investigated; mitigation (rollback of recent model/kernel changes) has been completed and normal service has been restored. We will provide a full post-incident report within 5 business days and an interim update in ~2 hours.
```

Sarah: LGTM. suggest we add impacted customer note: some long-running streaming sessions may have been interrupted; tokenization/partial outputs may have been lost.

Mike: approved to post interim status. Jordan please coordinate with customer-success for account-level outreach to top impacted tenants. add @Jordan to follow up thread.

Jordan: on it — will send account pings to affected customers and include recommended next steps: retry, if persistent open support ticket.

Ana: for the postmortem, I propose owners/initial action items:
- Root cause analysis (Ana + Sarah) — reproduce and confirm race condition in new packing path (target 3 business days)
- Hotfix + regression test (Sarah) — create unit + e2e tests, land safety check to prevent kv pointer reuse (target 5 business days)
- Observability improvements (Lee) — add metric for cache-eviction bursts and alert tuning (2 business days)
- Deployment gating (Mike) — add rollout canary policy change to stop kernel/model combo rollouts without passing perf smoke (1 business day)
- Customer comms (Jordan) — initial outreach + scheduled full RCA email draft (48 hours for initial; 5 business days for full RCA)

Mike: that looks good. assigning: Ana (RCA lead), Sarah (fix + tests), Lee (obs), Mike (rollout policy), Jordan (comms). please update the incident action tracker and add links to PRs once available.

Jordan: drafting customer email now — suggested subject: "Update: brief service disruption in eastus — interim status". body draft below for review:
```
Hi —
We experienced a service disruption affecting requests routed through our eastus serving pool between 19:30–20:12 UTC. We have rolled back the recent model/kernel changes that contributed to increased latency and 502s and normal service has been restored. We are actively investigating the root cause and will share a full Root Cause Analysis within 5 business days. If you saw interrupted streaming or partial outputs, please retry or open a support ticket and we'll prioritize assistance.
Thanks,
Redwood Inference Support
```

Sarah: minor wording tweak: change "model/kernel changes" to "an internal runtime packing change deployed with the model rollout" — a bit clearer for technical customers.

Jordan: updated. adding a small FAQ line for self-service retries. will send to customer-success for prioritization.

Lee: ops request — add follow-up note to statuspage once RCA is posted, with link to postmortem and list of action items. also recommend we add a short trust note about timeline to remediate and tests being added.

Mike: schedule postmortem meeting: propose 3pm UTC two business days from now — gives engineers time to reproduce and prep slides. is that ok?

Ana: 3pm UTC works. I'll prepare a timeline + reproduction notes.

Sarah: I'll bring a proposed patch for the fix and a test plan.

Jordan: I'll prepare the customer-facing RCA skeleton and share slides for review before the meeting.

Mike: good. Action item recap in thread (owner — due):
- Postmortem meeting scheduled (Mike) — 1945856000 (3pm UTC two business days)
- RCA reproduction + root cause writeup (Ana + Sarah) — due in 3 business days
- Hotfix + tests (Sarah) — 5 business days
- Observability metrics & alerts (Lee) — 2 business days
- Deployment gating change (Mike) — 1 business day
- Customer initial outreach (Jordan) — within 2 hours (posted)
- Full customer RCA email (Jordan) — 5 business days

Jordan: interim status posted to statuspage and pings sent to top-10 affected accounts. added support ticket tag "sev1-eastus-rollback" for any related follow-ups.

Ana: I'll add a checklist entry to the incident tracker for "verify no KV pointer reuse in packing path" and link the reproducer.

Mike: thanks team. Let's use this thread to track blockers; update the tracker and drop PR links here when you have them. We'll close the incident thread after the postmortem meeting and the customer RCA is published. :white_check_mark:

Lee: one more ask — ops wants a short blameless summary for legal/compliance saying the cause, mitigation, and that no customer data was exfiltrated. Jordan, can you draft that section for inclusion in the RCA?

Jordan: yep — will include a "customer data impact" section: currently no evidence of data leak, only transient request losses. will include confirmation after support validates.

Mike: perfect. closing notes: keep updates concise here, prioritize reproducer and fix PR. thanks everyone for quick response. :raised_hands:
